name: @topcoat-spike/dom-contract-vendor
description: Pinned upstream toolchain the dom-expressions contract extractors run against. Every version is exact -- zero ranges -- so a re-run either reproduces the committed fixtures or reports drift.
$note-babel-internals: @babel/traverse and @babel/generator are FORCED to the versions in upstream's
pnpm-lock at 56bd405. They are transitive deps of @babel/core, and yarn would
otherwise hoist newer ones that satisfy core's caret ranges.
This is load-bearing for byte-matching: Scope.generateUid lives in traverse,
and its numbering changed after 7.23 -- a newer traverse emits _tmpl$0/_el$0
where the committed fixtures have _tmpl$10/_el$10. Same identifiers, different
names, so every downstream reference differs too.
$note-prettier: prettier is pinned to 2.8.2 and babel-plugin-tester to 10.1.0 -- the exact
versions in the upstream repo's pnpm-lock at 56bd405. This is NOT optional
trivia: babel-plugin-tester formats every fixture output.js through prettier
before writing it, so the committed expected outputs are prettier-2.8.2
artifacts. Reproducing them byte-for-byte (G0 proof 3) requires the same
prettier major AND the repo's .prettierrc. See CONTRACT-DOM.md point 1.
$note-jsdom: jsdom is deliberately NOT a dependency. It was in the original spec, but:
(a) nothing here needs a live DOM -- the tree oracle is parse5-only and
trace.mjs is a synthetic recorder that must NOT touch a real DOM;
(b) jsdom >=30 requires node ^24.15.0 (this env is 24.5.0); and
(c) jsdom >=30 depends on parse5 ^8, which would put a SECOND parse5 major
in the tree. The oracle must use the same parse5 the reference plugin
uses (^7.1.2) or the two can disagree on HTML tree construction.
If a live DOM is ever needed, add jsdom@26 (parse5 7) rather than 30.
